questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem for an Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs
questions.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the missing coefficients in the solution to the initial value problem, shown above.

$x(t)=$ 
{{field-1}} 
$\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]\,+$
{{field-2}}
$\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
We are told that the general solution to the system is 

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

where ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}$  are constants that are to be determined. 

Next, we find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2(0)) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2(0))\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2(0)) \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2(0))\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-2(0)}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{2} \\ 2{c}_{1}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{2}=4 \\ 2{c}_{1}=1\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get ${c}_{2}=4.$ From the second equation, we have ${c}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
x(t)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+4\cdot [\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Form of a Particular Solution for Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs
questions.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}3{t}^{2}-t \\ -2{t}^{2}+4\end{aligned}]
$$

A complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$ where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{t}^{2}-t \\ -2{t}^{2}+4\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is a polynomial in $t$ of degree $2.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also a polynomial of degree $2$, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={t}^{2}[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{c}_{1},{c}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined.

questions.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]x(t)+{e}^{-5t}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 7\end{aligned}].
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{2t} \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system is

| $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+$ {{field-1}} $\cdot \,\,$ |  | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $-1$ |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
{e}^{-5t}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 7\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is exponential. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also exponential, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={e}^{-5t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}],
$$

where $a,b$  are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=-5{e}^{-5t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5{e}^{-5t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {e}^{-5t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-5t}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ -5[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-5a \\ -5b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2a+b \\ 2b\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-5a \\ -5b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2a+b+8 \\ 2b+7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2a+b+8=-5a \\ 2b+7=-5b\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get 

$$
2b+7=-5b\,⇒\,b=-1.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $a,$ we have

$$
2a+(-1)+8=-5a\,⇒\,a=-1.
$$

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={e}^{-5t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-9 & 12 \\ -8 & 11\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}-3t-12 \\ -8t-8\end{aligned}]
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system is

| $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | $\,\,t+\,\,$ |  | $-25$ |  | . |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $16$ |  |  | {{field-2}} |  |  |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3t-12 \\ -8t-8\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is polynomial of degree $1.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also polynomial of degree $1,$ i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2}$  are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9 & 12 \\ -8 & 11\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}])+[\begin{aligned}-3t-12 \\ -8t-8\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9({a}_{1}t+{b}_{1})+12({a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}) \\ -8({a}_{1}t+{b}_{1})+11({a}_{2}t+{b}_{2})\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3t-12 \\ -8t-8\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0t+{a}_{1} \\ 0t+{a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}(-9{a}_{1}+12{a}_{2}-3)t+(-9{b}_{1}+12{b}_{2}-12) \\ (-8{a}_{1}+11{a}_{2}-8)t+(-8{b}_{1}+11{b}_{2}-8)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-9{a}_{1}+12{a}_{2}-3=0 \\ -8{a}_{1}+11{a}_{2}-8=0 \\ -9{b}_{1}+12{b}_{2}-12={a}_{1} \\ -8{b}_{1}+11{b}_{2}-8={a}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first two equations, we get 

$$
{a}_{1}=21,\,{a}_{2}=16.
$$

 
Substituting these into the third and fourth equations, and solving for ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2},$ we have

$$
{b}_{1}=-25,\,{b}_{2}=-16.
$$

 

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}21 \\ 16\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}-25 \\ -16\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}-7\operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t) \\ 18\operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t)\end{aligned}],\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the missing coefficients in the solution to the initial value problem, shown above.

$x(t)=$ 
{{field-1}} 
$\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,+$
{{field-2}}
$\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t) \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t)\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
We are told that the general solution to the system is 

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t) \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t)\end{aligned}]
$$

where ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}$  are constants that are to be determined. 

Next, we find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{0} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}(0){e}^{0} \\ {e}^{0}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6(0))-\operatorname{sin}⁡(6(0)) \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡(6(0))\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+1 \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+1=2 \\ {c}_{2}=5\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get ${c}_{1}=1.$ From the second equation, we have ${c}_{2}=5.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
x(t)=1\cdot [\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+5\cdot [\begin{aligned}t{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t) \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t)\end{aligned}].
$$
